analysis.summary: The platform's only working deployment path today is Docker Compose (3 variants: dev, prod, atlas); no Kubernetes manifests, Helm chart, or CI build/push/deploy step exist anywhere in the repo. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md's 'Kubernetes' section is illustrative sample YAML, not a real deployable path. This is a net-new infrastructure/documentation build-out, not a bugfix, and the container image (server/Dockerfile.unified) and health endpoint are already containerization-ready and would not need application-code changes.
analysis.details: Architecture fit: the app is already packaged as a single stateless container image with an externalized env-var contract (server/src/config/env.ts) and a health endpoint (GET /api/health), which map cleanly onto a Kubernetes Deployment + ConfigMap/Secret + liveness/readiness probe. Extension points: the existing 3-variant Docker Compose split (dev/prod/atlas) is a direct precedent for a Kustomize base+overlays structure (or a parameterized Helm chart) covering the same environment variants, including the Atlas-external-Mongo toggle already proven in docker-compose.atlas.yml. Data flow / stateful concerns: the server/data/.seeded marker file (used to gate first-run seeding, persisted via a named volume in Compose) needs a PVC or alternative idempotency mechanism under Kubernetes. Prior art: the recently merged branding-profile feature (PR #10) added BRANDING_PROFILE/APP_NAME/ORG_NAME/ORG_URL env passthrough to docker-compose.prod.yml/atlas.yml — any Kubernetes ConfigMap/Secret scheme must replicate this same passthrough pattern. No genuine code-level dependency was found between this issue and the catalog-data issues (#5-#8); it is orthogonal and could technically be started independently, though it is the largest and most architecturally invasive change of the group.

options.name: Plain per-environment manifest sets
options.summary: Hand-write full YAML manifests per environment (k8s/prod/*.yaml, k8s/atlas/*.yaml) with no shared base or templating tool.

files_to_modify.changes: Document manual manifest apply steps per environment

pros: Zero new tooling, easiest to review line-by-line
cons: Reproduces the exact env-block duplication problem the Compose files already have across variants
Highest drift risk as env.ts grows
Contradicts the repo's own history of consolidating such duplication (branding PRs #3/#10)
options.risk_details: Manual duplication across environment manifest sets, no shared base to keep them in sync

options.name: Kustomize overlays (base + dev/prod/atlas)
options.summary: One base manifest set (Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, optional StatefulSet+PVC for self-hosted MongoDB) plus overlays mirroring the existing docker-compose.yml/.prod.yml/.atlas.yml split.

files_to_modify.changes: Document Kubernetes as the primary deployment path with kustomize apply instructions
Point to the new Kubernetes-primary guide
Update Deployment section to lead with Kubernetes
Add build-and-push-image job for the container registry

files_to_create.purpose: Environment-specific Kustomize overlays mirroring the 3 Compose variants

pros: kubectl-native, no new templating engine to learn

cons: Less reusable than Helm if the platform needs to be installed as a redistributable chart for third parties
options.risk_details: Large surface area (new k8s/ manifests, CI image pipeline, doc rewrite) but follows an existing, well-understood pattern in the repo

options.name: Helm chart
options.summary: Package a single parameterized Helm chart (values.yaml) covering the app Deployment/Service/Ingress, optional Mongo subchart or Atlas external-URI toggle, and branding profile as chart values.

files_to_create.purpose: Helm chart templates + values.yaml covering all deployment variants

pros: Single versioned chart, easy per-deployment overrides
Aligns naturally with the just-merged branding-profile feature
Good for distributing to multiple downstream operators
cons: Adds a new tool/dependency (Helm) the repo doesn't use anywhere today
Harder to review/diff than plain YAML given no CI pipeline validates manifests yet

decision_record.root_cause: The platform's only working deployment path is Docker Compose (3 variants); no Kubernetes manifests, Helm chart, or CI build/push/deploy step exist anywhere, so making Kubernetes the primary deployment path is a net-new infra/documentation build-out, not a fix to broken code.

options_rejected.reason: Reproduces the env-duplication problem the Compose files already have, contradicting the repo's own consolidation history
Introduces a new toolchain (Helm) with no prior art or test coverage in this repo

selected_option.name: Kustomize overlays (base + dev/prod/atlas)
selected_option.summary: Mirror the existing 3-variant Docker Compose split with a Kustomize base + overlays structure, kept kubectl-native.

decision_record.residual_risk: No test coverage or CI validation exists for any manifests; correctness of the K8s ConfigMap/Secret env contract vs. server/src/config/env.ts must be verified manually. Per project decision, this issue is deliberately isolated into its own PR/branch and held for manual merge — it must not be combined with any other issue's changes.
